When Temüjin is nine, his father Yesügei takes him to another tribe, to find him a future wife.

Without a chief, the clan does something brutal. They pack up, take the herds, and leave.
Temüjin, his mother Höelun and her children are abandoned on the open steppe.
Temoojin, his mother Hoh-eh-loon, and her children are abandoned on the open steppe.
On the steppe, that was supposed to be a death sentence.
They survive anyway. They eat roots, berries, wild onions, fish from the river, and anything Temüjin and his brothers can shoot.

Quick side quest.
Even with a clan around you, life on the steppe is hard.
Families live in round felt tents called gers, which can be packed onto a cart in about an hour when it's time to move the herds.
Families live in round felt tents called gairs, which can be packed onto a cart in about an hour, when it's time to move the herds.
Kids learn to ride almost before they can walk, and by five or six they're shooting small bows from the saddle.
Everything depends on horses. You ride them, you trade them, and you drink their fermented milk, called airag.
Everything depends on horses. You ride them, you trade them, and you drink their fermented milk, called eye-rag.
Travelers later wrote that on long rides, Mongol warriors would even drink a little of their horse's blood to survive.
Höelun refuses to let her children give up. She reminds them who their ancestors were, that they are not nobodies.
Hoh-eh-loon refuses to let her children give up. She reminds them who their ancestors were, that they are not nobodies.
Years later, Temüjin will treat his mother's word almost like law.
Years later, Temoojin will treat his mother's word almost like law.
Then comes the darkest moment of his childhood.
His older half-brother, Begter, keeps taking the food they catch.
Temüjin and his brother Khasar hunt him down, and kill him with arrows.
Temoojin and his brother Kha-sar hunt him down, and kill him with arrows.
Their mother is furious. But inside that tiny family, there is now only one leader.
The clan that abandoned them hears that the boy is growing up, and decides to deal with him.
They capture Temüjin and lock his neck and wrists in a cangue, a heavy wooden collar, like a portable prison.
They capture Temoojin and lock his neck and wrists in a cang, a heavy wooden collar, like a portable prison.
One night, during a feast, he knocks out his guard with the collar, and runs.
He hides in a river, with only his face above the water.
A stranger spots him, and instead of calling the guards, hides him in a cart full of wool.
The searchers poke the wool with spears.
They miss.
He gets away. And he never forgets two things: who betrayed him, and who saved him.
